paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend: the brothers walk into Joseph's house sure they're headed for trouble. They say, "We have been brought here because of the silver that was returned in our bags the first time," and they expect to be taken as slaves (Genesis 43:18). Instead they get water for their feet, food for their donkeys and a seat at the table (Genesis 43:24, 33-34). Fear is LOUD, baker, but it doesn't always read the room right.

Look at Judah, too. His father is stuck, and Judah steps up and says, "I will guarantee his safety. You may hold me personally responsible" (Genesis 43:9). He even says that if he doesn't bring Benjamin back, he will bear the guilt before his father all his life (Genesis 43:9). That's what a real promise looks like, and I think it shows how God can work in a person who is willing to carry weight for someone else.

And then there's Jacob, who sends his youngest son down with gifts, double the silver and a prayer: "May God Almighty grant you mercy before the man" (Genesis 43:14). He couldn't see how it would turn out, so he handed it to God. You and I do that when we pray over something we can't fix. This story isn't done baking, so hang on to that, friend.
